passage: At 11:52 pm, eight minutes before the assignment portal closed, Vasudha's laptop froze on the loading circle. "No, no, no. You're doing this on purpose," she hissed at it in their hostel room in Pune. "You always pick deadline night." Parul looked up from her bunk. "It's a machine, Vasu." "It's a machine that hates me." Vasudha stroked the lid like a nervous pet. "Come on, Tortoise, please, just one upload. I'll clean your fan tomorrow, I promise." The circle spun, then the page loaded. "Good boy," she whispered, and clicked submit at 11:57. Parul laughed. "You named it Tortoise?" "Of course. If it has moods, at least I can bargain with it. If it's just random, I'm helpless."

"She's angry because you didn't wash her last week," Jatin said from the passenger seat, grinning. "She's angry because you slammed her door. Say sorry." "I'm not saying sorry to a car." It was eight degrees last night." "Maybe. But Rani starts better when you talk nicely." He pumped the pedal once, turned the key, and the engine caught. "Told you!" Jatin laughed. "Fine. Thank you, Rani ji. Now drive."

passage: I'm Akash, and during my internship I became the guy who talks to the office printer. It started in my second week. It jammed every time I had to print something for the manager, never for anyone else, or so it felt. "It can smell fear," I told Jahnavi, who sat next to me. She laughed, but I half meant it. I started greeting it. "Good morning, Kaka. Be kind today." I'd pat its side before big print jobs. Looking back, I think I needed it to have a personality. A printer that jams at random while your manager waits is terrifying. A printer that's grumpy is almost a colleague. Jahnavi eventually found the paper tray was bent and straightened it with a ruler. Kaka stopped jamming. I still said good morning to it, though. Old habits.

qa.q: What did Jahnavi find wrong with the printer?
qa.a: The paper tray was bent.

qa.q: Why did Akash feel better thinking of the printer as grumpy?
qa.a: A grumpy printer felt like almost a colleague Akash could handle, while random jams in front of the manager felt terrifying 😅

qa.q: What turned out to be the real fix, and what could Akash try sooner next time?
qa.a: Jahnavi straightened the bent tray with a ruler. Next time Akash could look for a physical cause early, while still enjoying the morning greeting.

qa.q: How might Jahnavi have seen Akash's habit of greeting Kaka?
qa.a: Jahnavi laughed but seemed fond of it, and helped in a practical way rather than mocking.

grounding: A young intern gives the office printer a name and moods, which makes its jams feel less random.

Lab supervisor's note, Manjula Iyer, microbiology lab, Year 2.
Shreya (20) has named our old centrifuge "Grumpy." She greets it each morning and pats its lid before a run. When it stalls, she says, "He hates Mondays," or "He's sulking because I forgot him on Friday." The others have picked this up; the whole bench now blames Grumpy's moods.
I noticed Shreya seems calmer since the naming. When it stalls, she laughs instead of panicking, and she said, "At least now I know why he does it." Her explanation is a story, but it seems to settle her.
Today I looked at the logbook. Every stall is on a Monday morning, when the building restarts the power. I'll show Shreya the pattern tomorrow, and keep the name. It's clearly helping.

qa.q: What has Shreya named the old centrifuge?
qa.a: She has named it "Grumpy."

qa.q: Why might Shreya say "At least now I know why he does it"?
qa.a: Giving the machine moods makes its stalls feel explained rather than random, which seems to calm her.

qa.q: What small step did Manjula plan, and why is it a good one?
qa.a: Showing Shreya the Monday power pattern gives a real cause, while keeping the name that helps the bench stay calm.

qa.q: How might the rest of the bench see Grumpy after Manjula shows the logbook?
qa.a: They might still joke about Grumpy's moods but also know to plan around the Monday restart.

grounding: A supervisor notes a young adult naming a lab machine and blaming its moods, which makes its failures feel explainable.

passage:
Tuesday night

Bijli did it again. Stopped dead at the Deccan signal, with a bus honking behind me. I patted her tank and said, "Come on, don't sulk, I washed you on Sunday." Kicked twice. Nothing. Third kick, she coughed and went. I swear she was punishing me for parking her in the sun all week.
Francis says she's a secondhand scooter with a dirty spark plug. Also says I'm mad for talking to her. But when I say she's in a mood, it at least makes sense to me. If it's just random, I'd go crazy at every signal.
Taking her to the mechanic on Saturday. I'll tell him she's been moody. He'll say spark plug. We'll both be right.
Samir
